style.name: String Art
style.description: Curve stitching on a nail board: a dark walnut-stained board (well lit, warm workshop light) with rows and a ring of brass nails; saturated cotton thread is wound nail to nail by a moving needle tip, each thread drawn up to the current point with a tiny wrap round every nail it turns on. Every thread is perfectly straight, yet together they make smooth curves — parabola fans between two nail rows, a cardioid from a ring (chords m -> 2m, wound as continuous doubling cycles). Threads stack in winding order, cast thin shadows on the board and catch a soft sheen; nails catch highlights. A winding planner (winding.js) is the single source of truth for picture and sound: a soft pluck per thread, pitch rising with its index.
motion: Every thread is a straight segment from nail to nail; the curve is only the envelope of many of them.
A needle tip draws each thread up to the current point (eased when slow, linear when fast) and lifts in a small arc between threads.
Threads stack in winding order a hair apart and cast thin shadows, so crossings layer like real thread.
Ring figures (chords m -> 2m mod N, N odd) are wound as closed doubling cycles: one continuous thread per cycle.

beats.label: A few units: a rough bend

notes.mechanism: winding.js: nails laid out from two parabola fans (two nail rows from a corner) and a ring of 73; thread i of a fan joins row-V nail n-i to row-U nail i; the ring figure is chords m -> 2m mod 73, split into 8 closed doubling cycles of 9, each wound as one continuous thread. Each run spreads its segments over [t0, t1] by length (constant needle speed) plus hop costs; threads stack by start time.
